issue: téh₂es (fem. nom. pl.) resumes moysṓs, which is masculine (thematic moysós 'ram'); expected tóy. The text also switches between moysós and h₂ówis for 'sheep'.
bʰréh₂teres mért: plural subject with a 3sg verb; and mért is an uninflected lemma (root aorist 'died'), not a gnomic present (*mr̥yétor / 3pl *mr̥yóntor).

This is Schleicher's 1868 text, faithfully transcribed, but it is impossible as modern PIE: a-vocalism (akwāsas, wawakant, manus, patis for *h₁éḱwōs, *wéwkʷont, *mónus, *pótis), no laryngeals, no accents, ā 'and'. It is a historical artifact and should be tagged as such. avibʰyams is dat. pl., but the English has singular 'the sheep has'.
ph₂tḗr-kʷe méh₂tēr: -kʷe is on the first conjunct; expected ph₂tḗr méh₂tēr-kʷe (or -kʷe on both).

Lehmann-Zgusta (1979) notation: no laryngeals (owis, aǵrom for *h₂ówis, *h₂éǵrom), no accents, augmented ebʰuget. The morphology is otherwise sound, but it does not match the corpus's laryngealist standard or the other lines of the same fable.
h₂éwis means 'bird' (the lexicon and other items use it that way); 'sheep' is h₂ówis. The coordination is also defective: gʰóstis-kʷe gʷówes-kʷe h₂éwis leaves the last member without -kʷe.
sn̥h₂wé is PST.1DU ('we two swam'), but the subject is dʰǵʰúHes (3pl); expected sn̥h₂ént. Also dʰǵʰúHobʰos has a spurious thematic -o- in a root-noun dat. pl. (expected *dʰǵʰuHbʰós).
h₁uséwih₂: the fem. of the u-stem adjective is built on a full-grade suffix; expected *h₁wéswih₂ / *h₁uswíh₂ (cf. Skt vásvī, urvī́).
tā́s (fem. acc. pl.) resumes the masculine moysṓs ('then she ate them up'); expected tóns. (The tā́s in the moral is fine, since it resumes fem. h₂ówins.)
h₂élete is the 2pl/IMP.2PL form ('you nourish'), but the subject is wérǵom (3sg); expected h₂életi.
dʰéǵʰōm is used as the object, with the nom.-type lengthened grade; the acc. should be *dʰéǵʰom (or *dʰǵʰém). The engine paradigm wrongly sets ACC.SG = NOM.SG.
ḱlutṓys is the instr. pl. of ḱlutós. The predicate of h₁nómn̥ needs nom. sg. neuter ḱlutóm ('his name is famous').
